newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunis bourse more attractive to investors,chief says.
newsitem.headline: Tunis bourse more attractive to investors,chief says.

text.p: The Tunis Stock Exchange is set to become more attractive to investors with the transfer of all thirty one listed shares onto the computerised dealing system with its greater transparency and the adoption of international standards, the bourse's chief said on Wednesday.

"The computerised dealing system covers now all the listed shares. It has rationalised the market and made it more attractive for investors because the old times where prices were artificially supported are over," Ahmed Hadouej, chairman of the Tunis Stock Exchange told Reuters in an interview.

Hadouej said that as part of the programme to upgrade the stock market in line with international standards, the way the index is calculated will be reviewed by October to base it on market capitalisation. By August, investors will be able to monitor prices in real time.

Since last October, the Tunis bourse has been progressively introducing shares listed on the original market onto the new computerised dealing system. All 31 shares have been transferred to the new system.

The bourse has been also been privatised, new rules have been introduced to encourage more listings, a central share depositary and a guarantee fund were established. Foreign ownership of listed stocks has been freed up and the ownership ceiling lifted to 49 percent from 10 percent.
As the modernisation programme was implemented, the bourse index fell. It dropped by 20.5 percent during the first half of 1997, and by 10.08 percent in 1996.
"This is a technical adjustment since you have changed the system," Hadouej said.

"Most important is the rise in volume traded on the (original) market which rose by 41 percent to 161.57 million dinars during the first half of 1997 compared to 114.38 million dinars during the same period in 1996," he added.
Total volume including over-the-counter deals rose by 26 percent to 314.57 million dinars compared to 250.24 million dinars.

"With the new system, you get the real price of the market. Before the modernisation, there was no transparency, and brokers were dealing between themselves. Now they deal with the market," Hadouej added.
"We have reached our two main goals: transparency, and liquidity," he added, insisting that the market's rules must be implemented to make the Tunis Stock Exchange gain in credibility.

"As share prices fall, the Price Earnings Ratio (P/E Ratio) becomes very interesting for investors. Before the computerised dealing system, we had ratios of over 60. They are now closer to international standards," Hadouej said.
Best P/Es on the exchange are those of Tunisie Lait at 7.0, Alkimia at 8.0, Airline Tunis Air and ICF at 9.0, UBCI and BNA bank at 10, SPCD and Le Moteur at 11.
Tunisie Leasing, STB bank, Banque de l'Habitat, UIB bank, Carte insurance, BTEI bank and BDET bank are at 12.

Hadouej said he expected three new firms to be listed this month on the Exchange -- insurance firm STAR which is expected to float a 20 percent stake, Arab Tunisian Lease (ATL), and Compagnie Internationale de Leasing (CIL).
The index closed at 455.13 on Wednesday. ($=1.1062 dinar)
